TL;DR

title: Nashville Housing Purchasing App
text:
Problem
I moved to Nashville around 2022 and was interested in home ownership, both for living and for real estate investing. The goal was to give prospective buyers data-driven analysis of the market so they can identify the best deal for them.

title: Nashville Housing Purchasing App
text:
Data
Nashville housing data on Kaggle. The quality and quantity of this data limit the predictions.

title: Nashville Housing Purchasing App
text:
Approach

Model: random forest in R, updated from the user’s inputs.
App: R Shiny (UI, server and reactivity), ggplot visualizations, and R Markdown report generation.
Design: Figma mockups (PDF).

How a user moves through the app:

Read the home page description.
Explore descriptive visualizations of Nashville housing.
Enter a housing profile on the deal prediction tab; the model updates dynamically and returns a prediction.
Generate an HTML/PDF report with all visualizations and the deal prediction insights.

title: Nashville Housing Purchasing App
text:
Results
The app delivers deal predictions based partly on the user’s inputs, plus a downloadable report. It is a prototype and is not currently maintained.

title: Nashville Housing Purchasing App
text:
What I’d Do Next / Limitations

R Shiny is a strong framework for rapid prototyping of apps that include statistics and machine learning models.
Predictions are limited by the quantity and quality of the Kaggle data.

title: Bank Personal Loan Analysis
text:
Problem
Banks run loan marketing campaigns and need to decide whom to target. This project builds a propensity model from past campaign results to answer:

What factors influence a customer’s likelihood to accept a loan offer?
How can customer targeting be improved to increase acceptance rates?

title: Bank Personal Loan Analysis
text:
Data
Past campaign results with customer attributes and whether the customer accepted the loan.

title: Bank Personal Loan Analysis
text:
Approach

Explore and clean the data to find patterns in customer behavior.
Analyze relationships between customer variables and loan acceptance.
Run A/B testing for experimentation.
Fit logistic regression and XGBoost, with feature engineering.
Compare the models with visualizations.

Logistic regression is a transparent baseline for a binary outcome; XGBoost is a stronger non-linear alternative.

title: Bank Personal Loan Analysis
text:
Results

Identified the key factors influencing loan acceptance.
Feature engineering improved model predictions.
XGBoost outperformed the traditional models in predictive accuracy.



Business Impact

Ranking customers by predicted propensity lets a marketing team focus offers on the likeliest acceptors instead of contacting everyone.

title: Bank Personal Loan Analysis
text:
What I’d Do Next / Limitations

Check probability calibration, so that scores can be used as acceptance probabilities and not only as a ranking.
Test the model on a campaign it wasn’t built from.

title: Cancer Mortality Analysis
text:
Problem
I picked this topic because of personal family ties to cancer. The goal was to understand what drives cancer mortality at the county level, so that public health initiatives can be guided by data. The analysis asks:

What are the primary causes of cancer mortality?
Which risk factors contribute to higher mortality rates at the county level?

title: Cancer Mortality Analysis
text:
Data
County-level data, about 3,000 rows and 34 variables, covering roughly 2015.

title: Cancer Mortality Analysis
text:
Approach

Explore and clean the data.
Prepare the data for machine learning models.
Apply regression analysis and machine learning techniques (Python).
Evaluate and interpret the results, and summarize the findings.

title: Cancer Mortality Analysis
text:
Results

XGBoost outperformed the other models in predictive accuracy.
Hyperparameter tuning improved accuracy but was time-intensive.
Data quality and preprocessing played a major role in improving results.

title: Cancer Mortality Analysis
text:
What I’d Do Next / Limitations

Add cross-validation to make the model comparison more reliable. This is the next iteration.
Stacking models significantly increased compute time.

TL;DR

title: Munay Works: AI Platform for Nonprofit Funding
text:
Problem
Nonprofits have to find funders that fit their mission and then write about their work in ways those funders respond to. The public data to support this exists as IRS Form 990 filings, but it’s large and hard to use directly. Munay Works is an AI-enabled platform that helps nonprofits find funders and generate grant insights from that data. I’m building it independently, and this page covers the technical work.

title: Munay Works: AI Platform for Nonprofit Funding
text:
Architecture






flowchart TD
  A["990 sources<br/>GivingTuesday data lake<br/>IRS TEOS monthly files"] --> B["ETL / ingestion"]
  B --> C[("PostgreSQL / Supabase<br/>source tables + analytics tables<br/>pgvector")]
  C --> D["RAG pipeline<br/>+ multi-agent layer<br/>(LangChain, FAISS)"]
  D --> E["FastAPI"]
  E --> F["React app"]






Stack: React · Python / FastAPI · LangChain · RAG pipeline · multi-agent architecture · FAISS · pgvector · PostgreSQL / Supabase

title: Munay Works: AI Platform for Nonprofit Funding
text:
Data Pipeline

Sources: 990 filings from the GivingTuesday data lake, and the IRS TEOS monthly files.
Two-layer PostgreSQL schema: source tables are kept separate from analytics tables, so raw filings stay untouched and the analytics layer can be rebuilt.
Materialized views provide peer benchmarks and foundation profiles.
Organization health score: a 100-point score computed for each organization.

title: Munay Works: AI Platform for Nonprofit Funding
section: AI Layer and How Outputs Are Evaluated
text:
AI Layer and How Outputs Are Evaluated
The AI layer is a RAG pipeline with a multi-agent architecture. LangChain orchestrates it, and retrieval uses FAISS and pgvector over the data above, so answers are grounded in actual filings and not generated from the model alone.

title: Munay Works: AI Platform for Nonprofit Funding
text:
What Pilots Taught Me
The platform is in a pilot with nonprofit organizations, and user feedback from the pilot drives the roadmap. 

Lessons From the Early Prototype
The first version, built in late 2025, was a Streamlit app using LangChain and FAISS. It pulled nonprofit data from the ProPublica API (IRS Form 990), and offered two modes: an advisory mode for grant-writing strategy, and a document mode where a user uploads an RFP, retrieves from it, and drafts responses. What carried forward:

Clearly separating the advisory and document modes improved the user experience.
RAG relevance depends on high-quality chunking and metadata.
Local model support balances privacy and performance tradeoffs.

title: Munay Works: AI Platform for Nonprofit Funding
text:
What’s Next

The roadmap follows what pilot users ask for.
